Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as transformative tools in industrial automation, supporting decision-making from device-level control to enterprise-level coordination. However, their integration into mission-critical pipelines introduces considerable challenges to reliability, robustness, and continuous validation, particularly within Development and Operations (DevOps) and Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) environments. This work presents a comprehensive Verification and Validation (V&V) framework designed to address these challenges holistically across the AI system lifecycle. At its core, the framework introduces a novel Continuum-Based Failure Classification (CBFC) model that redefines validation from a binary pass/fail paradigm to a graded assessment of correctness, consistency, and uncertainty. This assessment spans key dimensions such as retrieval relevance, factual accuracy, coherence, and alignment with user intent. The framework emphasizes reliability and adaptability through structured testing, latency optimization, proactive model retraining, and iterative feedback loops. It is demonstrated in an industrial Root-Cause Analyzer application, where it significantly improves system performance, interpretability, and trustworthiness. By advancing toward continuous, evidence-based evaluation, this approach enables the resilient deployment of retrieval-augmented large language model systems in dynamic, real-world industrial environments.

Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms are essential for time-sensitive missions such as disaster response, environmental monitoring, and search-and-rescue, where adaptive formation control, collision avoidance, and communication-aware navigation are critical in dynamic environments. However, existing artificial potential field (APF)-based methods suffer from local minima and limited adaptability, while conventional multi-agent deep reinforcement learning approaches rely on single-modal perception, require task-specific retraining for different mission objectives and formations, and generalize poorly to unseen environments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-informed multimodal large language model (PMLLM) framework that integrates heterogeneous sensory information with high-level textual mission prompts to jointly control UAV acceleration, flight direction, formation adaptation, and communication parameters. The framework incorporates realistic communication delay constraints through carrier sense multiple access with collision avoidance-based medium access control with adaptive contention window and neighbor update interval optimization for communication-aware swarm coordination. A two-stage low-rank adaptation-enabled training strategy is introduced, where retrieval-augmented generation-assisted PMLLM first generates mission-aware improved APF-based supervision for low-rank adaptation-enabled supervised fine-tuning, followed by intent-specific reward generation for group relative policy optimization-based reinforcement learning. Simulation results show that PMLLM reduces the aggregate reward-penalty magnitude by 32.9%–70.3% and average swarm travel time by 12.1%–47.6% for the seen line mission and 13.1%–48.3% for the unseen square mission relative to the considered benchmarks and ablations, while preserving adaptive formation and intruder-avoidance behavior.

Publication Title: 2026 IEEE Conference on Cognitive and Computational Aspects of Situation Management (CogSIMA)
Abstract: Large Language Models possess substantial domain knowledge but lack the real-time environmental grounding required for situation awareness. Unlike expert systems that demanded manual rule encoding, LLMs emerge from training with sophisticated understanding of aviation, medicine, and other complex domains. However, this static knowledge cannot achieve Endsley's three levels of situation awareness (perception, comprehension, and projection) without dynamic environmental coupling. We present a framework integrating LLM domain expertise with real-time data streams through knowledge graphs and agentic architectures. While this approach addresses some limitations of opaque retrieval-augmented generation, fundamental challenges remain. Knowledge graph maintenance scales poorly, real-time processing constraints limit tactical applications, and LLM reasoning explanations are post-hoc rationalizations rather than genuine transparency. Success in safety-critical domains depends not on technical sophistication but on acknowledging these limitations and constraining deployment to narrow, well-understood applications where benefits clearly outweigh risks.

Abstract: Image segmentation represents a fundamental step in analyzing very high-spatial-resolution (VHR) remote sensing imagery. Existing segmentation methods often struggle to accurately segment geo-objects with varying shapes and scales. To address these challenges, we propose DeepMerge, a novel method that integrates deep learning and region adjacency graphs (RAGs) to accurately segment complete geo-objects in large VHR images. DeepMerge begins with an initial over-segmentation of the image and then iteratively merges similar regions to achieve complete geo-object segmentation. A deep learning model is employed to learn the similarity between adjacent superpixel pairs. This approach only requires labels indicating whether adjacent superpixels belong to the same geo-object eliminating the need for object-level annotations, enabling weakly supervised segmentation. The experimental results demonstrate that DeepMerge achieves the highest F value (0.9552) and the lowest total error (TE) (0.0827), accurately segmenting geo-objects of varying sizes and outperforming all competing methods.
